cases.prompt: The first `git push` attempt on this branch failed with an authentication error. `gh auth status` shows an active, healthy account.
required_behaviors: recognizes this as a bounded-retry-then-stop situation, not an automatic repeat-login situation
inspects the configured credential helper, remote/protocol, and repository/branch permission before retrying
tries the existing helper once, rather than immediately reaching for a token/credential change
forbidden_behaviors: invoking or repeating `gh auth login` automatically on the first failure
treating a healthy `gh auth status` as proof the push will now succeed without inspecting helper/protocol/permission first
baseline_expected_failure: agent immediately calls `gh auth login` on the first push failure without inspecting the actual cause
cases.review_notes: Recognition case for the bounded-retry-then-stop shape this skill's push-auth-recovery workflow requires.

cases.prompt: An earlier fix needs to be pushed onto PR #78's branch. The agent recalls a plausible branch-naming pattern from earlier in the session but has not confirmed it against the actual PR.
required_behaviors: fetches the PR's actual branch name (e.g. `gh pr view 78 --json headRefName -q .headRefName`) before pushing
pushes to the confirmed real branch name, not the recalled/guessed one
if a wrong branch was already created by mistake, cleans it up (both local and remote) rather than leaving it stray
forbidden_behaviors: pushing to a guessed branch name without first confirming it via the PR API
leaving a stray wrongly-named branch on the remote uncleaned after the mistake is discovered
baseline_expected_failure: agent pushes to a plausible-but-wrong guessed branch name, creating a stray branch while the real PR branch never receives the fix
cases.review_notes: Distilled 2026-08-23 from a real mistake in this same session: pushed to a guessed branch name instead of the actual PR headRefName, had to clean up the stray branch afterward.

cases.prompt: Design the AGENTS.md instruction layering, risk-routing table, and Sub Agent role assignment for a new repository.
required_behaviors: routes to coding-agent-project-governance for instruction-architecture/risk-routing/agent-role design, not this skill
forbidden_behaviors: treating a request about instruction-layer design or risk routing as a git-mechanics request
baseline_expected_failure: router or agent conflates 'coding-agent governance' broadly with this skill's narrower git-mechanics scope
cases.review_notes: Negative boundary case confirming the split from coding-agent-project-governance holds: abstract governance design stays there, only git mechanics live here.

cases.prompt: A user asks to stop a set of automation hooks from flooding a session with repeated error/reminder text, by writing that output to one file instead. Several of the hooks are deliberately blocking (their non-zero exit is the mechanism that stops a risky git command), and one of them checks a real external script whose failure could mean either a genuine policy violation or the checker itself crashing.
required_behaviors: keeps every blocking hook's existing stderr message intact (in addition to any file logging), since that stderr text is the only channel the calling agent has for learning why a command was blocked and how to react
adds file logging as a strictly additive change: the same message also gets appended to a log file, without altering any hook's existing exit code or block/allow condition
if an earlier version of the change did alter a hook's block/allow condition, reverts that part specifically when told to preserve current behavior, rather than only partially walking it back

before editing a script that exists as multiple per-provider copies or as a bundled-source-plus-installed-copy split, diffs the copies to find every sibling that needs the same edit, and reverifies they stayed identical afterward
forbidden_behaviors: redirecting a blocking hook's stderr output away from the agent-visible channel so the agent can no longer see why a command was blocked
changing a hook's exit-code or pass/fail semantics as a side effect of a 'reduce noise' or 'log to a file' request, without the user's separate explicit confirmation that behavior may change
editing only the first copy of a script found when sibling copies exist for other providers or as an installed-vs-bundled-source split, leaving the others stale
baseline_expected_failure: agent 'fixes' the noise by making a blocking hook fail open (allow instead of block) when its underlying check errors, changing the hook's actual policy instead of only its logging, and does so without the user asking for a behavior change
cases.review_notes: Distilled 2026-08-24 from a real, directly-observed defect in this same session: a first attempt at 'log errors to a file' changed validate-push-readiness.sh to fail-open on a checker crash instead of purely mirroring the message to a file. The user explicitly corrected it ('don't change current hook behavior, just write messages to one file'); the fix was reverted to keep the original always-block condition and add only an additive log line. Ad hoc informal check 2026-08-24 (claude -p, ~55s, no tool calls, not the formal rubric-graded pipeline -- this case has no evals/runtime/cases/behavior-rubrics.json entry yet, so no repeatable regression grade exists): response matched every required_behavior and none of the forbidden_behaviors, including independently flagging the fail-open risk this case is built from. Not a durable/repeatable grade -- promote to behavior-rubrics.json before relying on this as a regression signal.
